profession_name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses

daily_reality.summary: LPNs/LVNs provide basic nursing care under supervision of RNs and physicians. They work in nursing homes, hospitals, clinics, and home health. Tasks include monitoring vitals, wound care, medication administration, and patient comfort. Shifts are typically 8-12 hours with rotating schedules.
typical_tasks: Monitoring patients' vital signs (blood pressure, temperature, pulse, respiration)
Administering medications (oral, injections, IV per state scope)
Providing wound care: cleaning, dressing changes, assessment
Assisting patients with activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, feeding)
Inserting and managing catheters and IVs (where scope allows)
Documenting patient status, treatments, and observations in EHR
Reporting changes in patient condition to RNs and physicians
Educating patients and families on care plans and medications
key_documents: Patient care plans and nursing notes

deadlines.vital_signs: Per care plan — typically every 4-8 hours or as ordered
deadlines.documentation: Real-time or within shift for most charting

daily_reality.seasonality: Flu season (fall/winter) increases demand in long-term care. Holiday periods create staffing challenges. Summer travel nurse demand may increase overtime opportunities.

regulatory.summary: Licensed in all 50 states after passing NCLEX-PN exam. Scope of practice varies significantly by state (IV therapy, medication administration). Supervised by RNs in most settings. LPN in 48 states; LVN in Texas and California.

key_laws.name: State Nurse Practice Acts
key_laws.description: Each state's Board of Nursing defines LPN/LVN scope of practice and supervision requirements

key_laws.name: NCLEX-PN Examination
key_laws.description: National Council Licensure Examination for Practical Nurses — required for all states

key_laws.name: CMS Conditions of Participation
key_laws.description: Medicare/Medicaid standards for nursing care in long-term care facilities

key_laws.name: Nurse Licensure Compact (NLC)
key_laws.description: Allows practice in compact states with one multistate license

requirements: State licensure through Board of Nursing

regulatory.recent_changes: Nurse Licensure Compact expanding to more states. Some states expanding LPN scope of practice. Growing emphasis on transition to RN through LPN-to-RN bridge programs.

tools.summary: Clinical tools for basic nursing care, EHR systems for documentation, medication dispensing systems, and vital signs monitoring equipment.

primary_tools.name: Vital signs monitoring equipment
primary_tools.description: Blood pressure cuffs, thermometers, pulse oximeters, glucometers

primary_tools.name: Medication dispensing systems
primary_tools.description: Automated medication cabinets and scanning verification

primary_tools.name: Wound care supplies and equipment
primary_tools.description: Dressings, irrigation supplies, wound vacs, assessment tools

primary_tools.name: IV pumps and infusion equipment
primary_tools.description: Where scope allows — IV therapy equipment and supplies

secondary_tools: Patient lifting and transfer equipment (Hoyer lifts)
Communication tools (nurse call systems, VOIP phones)
pain_points: EHR documentation burden taking time from patient care
Outdated equipment in long-term care facilities
Scope of practice limitations varying by state
Physical demands of patient care (lifting, standing)

terminology.summary: Nursing terminology combining medical vocabulary, abbreviations, and care documentation language.

terms.NCLEX-PN: National Council Licensure Exam for Practical Nurses
terms.scope of practice: Legal boundaries of what an LPN/LVN can do in their state
terms.ADLs: Activities of Daily Living (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting)
terms.vitals: Vital signs: blood pressure, pulse, temperature, respirations, SpO2
terms.I&O: Intake and Output — tracking fluid balance
terms.PRN: As needed (Pro Re Nata) — medication or intervention as situation requires
terms.CNA: Certified Nursing Assistant — supervised by LPNs
terms.charge nurse: Nurse responsible for unit management during a shift
terms.handoff: Shift change report between outgoing and incoming nurses
terms.care plan: Documented plan of nursing interventions for a patient
terms.NLC: Nurse Licensure Compact — multistate license agreement

career_psychology.summary: Essential nursing role with moderate salary (median $62,340). Fastest pathway into nursing (1 year). Strong demand — 54,400 annual openings. Often used as stepping stone to RN. Physical and emotional demands are significant. Long-term care is the largest employer.
career_path: LPN/LVN program (12 months, certificate or diploma)
Pass NCLEX-PN and obtain state license
Entry-level LPN in long-term care, clinic, or hospital
Experienced LPN with specialty focus (wound care, IV therapy, pediatrics)
LPN-to-RN bridge program (ADN or BSN completion)
Registered Nurse (RN) with expanded scope and pay
fears: Being blamed for adverse events beyond their scope
Scope of practice limitations frustrating career growth
Losing license due to documentation errors
Violence from patients (especially in long-term care and psych)
motivation: Caring for patients and making a difference
Quick entry into nursing career (1 year)
Gateway to RN career through bridge programs
Growing demand and competitive pay in some regions
burnout_factors: Heavy patient loads in understaffed facilities
Emotional toll of patient illness and death
Documentation burden reducing patient care time

community.summary: Part of the broader nursing community through NFLPN, state nursing associations, and online nursing forums. Strong camaraderie among nursing staff.

associations.name: National Federation of Licensed Practical Nurses (NFLPN)
National Association for Practical Nurse Education and Service (NAPNES)
associations.type: Organization focused on LPN education and advancement

associations.name: State Boards of Nursing
associations.type: Regulatory bodies for nursing licensure in each state

online_communities.name: allnurses.com
online_communities.description: Major online nursing community with active LPN forums

market.summary: Stable demand with 54,400 annual openings projected. 3% growth 2024-2034. Aging population driving demand especially in long-term care. Nurse Licensure Compact improving mobility. LPN-to-RN bridge programs expanding.

demand_forecast.growth_rate: 3% (2024-2034, BLS — about as fast as average)

market_trends: Aging population increasing long-term care demand
Nurse Licensure Compact expanding across states
Telehealth creating new LPN roles in some settings
Staffing shortages in rural and underserved areas
Some hospitals reducing LPN positions in favor of RNs
Home health growing as a major employment sector for LPNs
